title: Location data sharing without consent
description: User's GPS position data is continuously captured and shared with the wearable device without explicit informed consent for location tracking purposes.
assumptions: User is aware of wearing the device but may not understand the extent of location data collection.

title: Personal identification through device usage
description: The act of wearing the device creates a persistent identifier that can be used to track and identify the user across different contexts and time periods.
assumptions: Device is uniquely identifiable and can be linked to specific individuals.

title: Unintended data collection
description: User may not be aware that sensitive health data (heart rate, step counts) is being continuously collected and transmitted to the device.
assumptions: User may not fully understand the data collection scope of the wearable device.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Sensor telemetry data (heart rate, GPS position, timestamps) transmitted from user to wearable device could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit.
assumptions: Data transmission may occur over unencrypted or partially encrypted channels.

title: Meta-data linking and identification
description: Meta-data about the data flow (timestamps, frequency, data types) could be used to link the user to specific activities and infer personal information.
assumptions: Meta-data is not adequately protected or anonymized during transmission.

title: Sensitive health data storage
description: Wearable device stores sensitive health data (heart rate, step counts) which could be accessed by unauthorized parties if device is compromised or lost.
assumptions: Device storage security may be insufficient to protect sensitive health information.

title: Unintended data retention
description: Device may retain health data beyond necessary retention periods without user knowledge or consent.
assumptions: Device has default retention policies that may not align with user privacy expectations.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Wearable device may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) regarding health data collection and storage.
assumptions: Device manufacturer may not have implemented full regulatory compliance measures.

title: Location and movement tracking via GPS data transfer
description: GPS traces transferred from wearable device to companion app enable tracking of user movement patterns, which could be used to infer sensitive information about user habits, routines, and potentially sensitive locations visited.
assumptions: GPS data contains location information that can be used to track user movement

title: Excessive personal data collection at source
description: Wearable device may collect and share more personal data than strictly necessary for the intended exercise session tracking function, including device ID and timestamps that could be used for tracking or profiling.
assumptions: Device collects all available sensor data including metadata

title: Personal data storage and potential re-disclosure at destination
description: Companion app receives and stores personal data (exercise sessions, GPS traces, device ID, timestamps) which could be accessed by unauthorized parties or used for profiling beyond the intended exercise tracking purpose.
assumptions: App stores data for future use and may share with third parties

title: Data interception during transit
description: Personal data in transit between wearable device and companion app could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or may occur over public networks

title: Data integrity during transfer
description: Personal data transferred from wearable device to companion app could be modified or tampered with during transit, potentially altering exercise session data, GPS traces, or timestamps.
assumptions: Data transmission may not have integrity protection mechanisms

title: Unawareness of data sharing implications
description: User may not be fully aware of the implications of sharing personal health data (calories, meals, weight) with the companion app, including potential secondary uses or data retention policies.
assumptions: User is making manual entries without full understanding of downstream processing

title: Data disclosure via metadata in transit
description: Metadata about the parties (user and app) in the data flow could be used to link or identify the user, potentially enabling tracking or profiling during data transmission.
assumptions: Data flows over network where metadata could be observed

title: Data breach at destination
description: The companion app may be compromised, leading to unauthorized access to the user's personal health data (calories, meals, weight) stored or processed by the app.
assumptions: App has storage or processing capabilities that could be breached

title: Health data transfer across system boundary
description: Personal health information (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) is transferred from the companion mobile app to the health log store, representing a data disclosure across a system boundary.

title: Health data storage without adequate access controls
description: The health log store may not have sufficient access controls to prevent unauthorized access to the stored health logs.

title: Health data loss during transfer
description: Health logs may be lost during the transfer from the companion mobile app to the health log store due to network issues or system failures.

title: Unintended health data disclosure
description: Health logs may be disclosed unintentionally during the transfer, such as through metadata leakage or unintended data exposure.

title: Location data in transit may expose metadata
description: GPS location traces with timestamps are transmitted across the network boundary. This data flow can expose location metadata (e.g., sender identity, timing patterns) that could be used to link or identify individuals, even if the primary location data itself is not intercepted.
assumptions: Assumes standard network transmission without encryption or metadata protection

title: Location data stored without appropriate access controls
description: The location history store may not have sufficient access controls to prevent unauthorized access to stored GPS location traces. This could allow unauthorized parties to retrieve sensitive location history data.
assumptions: Assumes the store is a centralized system with potential access control gaps

title: Excessive location data collection violates minimality principle
description: The companion mobile app may be collecting and transmitting more GPS location data than strictly necessary for its intended functionality, violating the minimality principle in data disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the app's design may not have been carefully reviewed for data minimality

title: Unintended Data Disclosure to Analytics Service
description: Health log data (calorie, weight, exercise logs) is transferred from storage to analytics service for health-condition analysis. If the analytics service is not the intended recipient or if the data is being shared more broadly than necessary, this represents an unintended disclosure of personal health data.
assumptions: Analytics service may have broader access than intended or may share data with third parties

title: Data in Transit Disclosure Risk
description: Personal health data flows across a network boundary during transit. This creates risk of interception, eavesdropping, or unauthorized access to sensitive health information while in transit between Health Log Store and Health Analytics Service.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without guaranteed encryption

title: Data Minimization Violation
description: Health Log Store transfers calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions for health-condition analysis. If the analytics service only requires specific data elements for its intended purpose, transferring all available log data may violate the minimality principle of data collection and sharing.
assumptions: Analytics service may not need all data elements for its analysis

title: Explicit disclosure of location history to analytics service
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) receives location history data from the Location History Store (DS2), constituting an explicit disclosure of personal data. This transfer may expose sensitive movement patterns and daily routines to a system that may not have appropriate safeguards for handling such personal data.

title: Data confidentiality risk during transit
description: Location history data in transit between DS2 and P3 could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive personal information about individuals' movements and routines.

title: Potential over-collection of location data
description: The Location History Store (DS2) may be sharing more location data than strictly necessary for the analytics service's purpose, potentially violating the minimality principle in data collection.

title: Profiling of individuals through inferred health insights
description: The Health Analytics Service infers health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags that may reveal patterns about individuals' health status. This could lead to profiling of individuals based on their health data, potentially creating insights about groups of individuals with similar health conditions.
assumptions: The analytics service processes individual health data to generate inferred insights that may be shared with the companion app.

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management for health data sharing
description: The Health Analytics Service may lack adequate cybersecurity risk management practices when sharing inferred health insights with the Companion Mobile App. This could lead to privacy risks if the data is intercepted or mishandled during transmission.
assumptions: Health data is sensitive and requires proper cybersecurity controls during sharing between systems.
uncertainty_note: Context [2] provides Nc.3 as a valid threat tree node for insufficient cybersecurity risk management.

title: Linking through metadata in data flow
description: The data flow itself may contain metadata about the parties involved (Health Analytics Service and Companion Mobile App) that could be used to link or identify individuals. This data-centric threat arises from the flow itself.
assumptions: Metadata about the data flow parties could be extracted and used for linking purposes.

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management at destination
description: The Companion Mobile App may lack adequate cybersecurity risk management practices when receiving and processing the inferred health insights. This could lead to privacy risks if the data is mishandled or exposed.
assumptions: The app processes the received health insights and may need proper security controls.
uncertainty_note: Context [2] provides Nc.3 as a valid threat tree node for insufficient cybersecurity risk management.

title: Excessive Data Sharing with Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Health Analytics Service shares full health and location datasets with third-party cloud provider, potentially violating minimality principle by transferring more personal data than strictly required for the analytics purpose.

title: Data in Transit - Metadata Exposure
description: Data flows in transit between Health Analytics Service and Cloud Hosting Provider may expose metadata about parties being used to link or identify them, enabling potential profiling or tracking across the boundary.

title: Third-Party Data Storage and Access
description: Cloud Hosting Provider receives and stores personal health and location data, creating risk of unauthorized access, data breaches, or data retention beyond necessary periods by the third-party entity.

title: Data Integrity at Destination
description: Cloud Hosting Provider may lack adequate integrity controls for stored personal data, creating risk of unauthorized modification, corruption, or tampering of health analytics data.
